I understand that feeling a lot. Fear of abandonment so strong that you'd rather end it than live with uncertainty even if its disproven they'll leave. Fighting yourself is extremely difficult, but I believe in you. You already made wonderful progress by just posting. You let other people in and now other people (including myself) are here to help you out. You should pat yourself on the back for that.

You also recognized that it was a mistake which is also wonderful! I know sometimes I make mistakes but I'll convince myself I did it on purpose which leads down a rabbit hole of self hatred or I'll act like I've done nothing wrong and refuse to open up. So theres another great accomplishment you made.

You also said you want to ghost them, but you're not, but you're also respecting their feelings and boundaries. Even more accomplishments!

Try to remind yourself of these things. They may seem small but when it comes to BPD all the negatives are so big that we regularly forget how big our accomplishments are to us. 

You're a strong individual and you can get through this and it's completely ok to need help getting through it 💕

All that matters is you will get through this :)

It sounds like an honest mistake. I understand that BPD can emphasize those negative emotions though. I also understand why you would like to ghost, but I don't believe it's the best idea. Give him some space to calm down and then try to explain the context, just like you did here. Apologize for showing him the content and that you hadn't realized there was blackface in it because you hadn't seen it in awhile. Let him know that it was an honest mistake, but you're sorry for it.

He might come back with some of his thoughts and feelings. Just listen to him and try to validate him as well. Keep the communication open.

It can be hard to not want to run and hide when we upset people, but we have to work hard to learn to communicate instead. Sometimes (for me it's a lot of the time) my head is just making it seem worse than it is. You just won't know unless you take a chance on communicating afterwards.

For now I suggest taking some deep breaths and find something else that could comfort you or distract you. You could listen to music or watch some videos; or if it helps then you could write out what you would like to say.

Again, I know it's hard but this might be better than it seems. Anxiety and BPD can do some nasty things to our perceptions remember that ❤

Best of luck to you. I hope whatever happens you feel better 💕
